data.content_ref: inline:The target's own second countercondition concedes the game away: it acknowledges that if 'pragmatic necessity can be framed as a non-inductive rule of survival rather than an inductive belief,' the contradiction dissolves. But this is not a hypothetical — it is Popper's actual position. Popper frames the preference for well-corroborated theories as a critical-rational choice grounded in the aim of truth-seeking, explicitly NOT as an inductive inference. By listing this as an open countercondition rather than recognizing it as Popper's stated solution, the target erects a straw-man version of Popperianism (one that conflates all practical reliance on past experience with 'practicing induction operationally') and then declares that straw man internally inconsistent. The argument thus begs the question: it assumes Popper's pragmatic preference IS inductive (the very point in dispute) to conclude that Popperianism is self-contradictory. No genuine performative contradiction exists, because there is no logical inconsistency between (a) holding that induction is unjustifiable and (b) choosing to act on critically-vetted theories for truth-aimed reasons — the latter does not require the former to be valid.
